title: Semi-Ordered Permutation
summary: Given a 0-indexed permutation of n integers, denoted as nums , transform it into a semi-ordered permutation where the first element is 1 and the last element is n by swapping adjacent elements.
statement: Given a 0-indexed permutation of n integers, denoted as nums , transform it into a semi-ordered permutation where the first element is 1 and the last element is n by swapping adjacent elements. The goal is to determine the minimum number of swaps required to achieve this configuration.
constraints: nums is a permutation of 1 through n.
One operation swaps two adjacent elements.
Return the minimum swaps needed to place 1 first and n last; other values may be in any order.
hints: Moving 1 left costs its zero-based index; moving n right costs n-1 minus its index.
If 1 begins to the right of n, their necessary crossing advances both goals in one swap.
Add the two distances and subtract one exactly when index(1) > index(n).
Every required displacement needs that many adjacent crossings, and the direct moves attain the lower bound with only the shared crossing counted once.
editorial: Every required displacement needs that many adjacent crossings, and the direct moves attain the lower bound with only the shared crossing counted once.

tests.explanation: Move one left once and four right once, for two adjacent swaps.
The one crosses four while moving left, so that same crossing also shifts four right; two swaps suffice.
